speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you've had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain along with difficulty wearing earrings. To better understand your symptoms, could you tell me exactly when these pain episodes occur and how long they last?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Eustachian Tube Dysfunction secondary to chronic ear infections and recent tympanoplasty.

The patient's shooting pain while eating (chewing) and discomfort with earrings, despite recent hearing improvement, strongly suggests Eustachian tube dysfunction affecting the post-auricular area and tympanic membrane. Given her history of chronic bilateral ear infections, this dysfunction likely stems from persistent inflammation or scarring.

REQUEST TEST: Audiometry (Repeat)
